title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-16
- Start: 10:00 AM PST
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (SE), Ava (CSM), Dr. Sarah, Rajiv, Emily, Tom

Summary:
Quick weekly sync to review latest quality evals from the pilot, discuss prompt-set regressions noticed in the last run, confirm guardrail adjustments, and agree next steps for the benchmark rerun and production-readiness checklist.

Topics:
- Prompt set updates and observed regressions
- Scoring rubrics and threshold tuning
- Guardrails and PII handling
- Deployment mode discussion (hosted vs dedicated for throughput)
- Next steps and action items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone good morning, thanks for joining. we'll kick off, um, quick agenda, review the quality dashboard and focus on the flagged regressions from last Friday's run.
[00:14] Dr. Sarah Thompson: morning, thanks Maya. we saw a drop in helpfulness on the discharge-summary prompts, about a 9% hit, curious what changed on your side.
[00:27] Liam Patel: yeah, quick context - we rolled a prompt normalization patch to reduce hallucinations in other prompts, but it looks like it interacted badly with the discharge templates. may have tightened the stop tokens too much.
[00:40] Rajiv Menon: right, we're seeing truncated recommendations mid-sentence, so clinicians are losing the last line.
[00:50] Emily Park: and from product side, that's a regression for our success metric, which is actionable-recommendation rate at 90% or above. we're at 81 this week.
[01:05] Liam Patel: mm-hmm, we tracked the exact commit in the run sheet - commit id rw-prompt-norm-1221 - the patch added a forced stop sequence earlier for safety, but it might be clipping long outputs.
[01:20] Tom Alvarez: quick compliance note - any change to generation that affects content could change our audit surface. we need the guardrail logs updated.
[01:30] Maya Chen: totally, we'll attach the guardrail audit. Ava, can you confirm the log retention policy for the POC?
[01:38] Ava Gomez: yes, logs retained 30 days by default for the pilot, full export available on request. Tom, we can push S3 export of the audit logs if you want to store them in your vault.
[01:50] Dr. Sarah Thompson: that would help the internal review. also, can you walk through the scoring - how you compute helpfulness and factuality?
[01:58] Liam Patel: sure. high level: we compute three primary metrics - helpfulness, factuality (we run an automated fact-checker against the EHR snippets), and safety. helpfulness is a weighted score from annotator labels plus syntactic checks. factuality is a mix of rule-based checks and model-based entailment, we've got threshold drift alerts when scores change >5%.
[02:20] Rajiv Menon: last run triggered the threshold drift alert. the annotator batch showed more partial matches for meds and dosages.
[02:30] Emily Park: were these results coming from the hosted Redwood API or your dedicated pool?
[02:35] Liam Patel: hosted. the pilot is on hosted with a fallback to dedicated during load tests, but we haven't switched yet. the model variant was rwd-47b-1.2q (quantized).
[02:49] Dr. Sarah Thompson: is it possible quantization introduced subtle tokenization differences? we've seen medication strings get split oddly before.
[02:56] Liam Patel: good call - quantization shouldn't change tokenization but different model variants sometimes have slightly different decoding quirks. we'll repro locally against the pre- and post-patch versions to isolate.
[03:08] Maya Chen: ok next, quick demo of the prompt set comparison tool - Liam, you had a diff?
[03:15] Liam Patel: yep, sharing screen - (screen share noise) - sorry transcript may say uh- - the main diff is we added an explicit STOP_TOKEN earlier and tightened the temperature from 0.9 to 0.7 for safety. you can see the sample outputs here: baseline had a full recommendation, patched one is cutoff at 2nd bullet.
[03:40] Emily Park: can we tune temperature per-route? some routes like summarization are fine at 0.7 but clinical recommendations need 0.9 to be comprehensive.
[03:49] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports per-route configs, you can set temperature, max_tokens, and prompt templates per endpoint. you can also pin to model version for the route so we avoid unexpected drift.
[04:05] Rajiv Menon: how easy is it to rollback to the previous prompt set? we want a quick rollback if the next run fails.
[04:11] Liam Patel: rollbacks are one-click in the console, we keep versions and tags. Canary deploys supported too so you can route 10% of traffic to a variant.
[04:21] Tom Alvarez: about guardrails - we need PII scrubbing before logs leave the pod. can Redwood apply client-side redaction?
[04:29] Maya Chen: we have prefix redaction and regex-based filters you can apply in the SDK. for stronger guarantees, we also offer client-side SDK hooks so you can do redaction before sending.
[04:40] Dr. Sarah Thompson: the annotators also noted hallucinated drug interactions in two cases - can that be flagged automatically?
[04:48] Liam Patel: yes, we can add a rule-based detector that flags when mention of drug A interacts with drug B and the confidence is low. we'll include that as an extra safety check in the pipeline.
[04:59] Emily Park: quick question about benchmark cadence - do you recommend rerunning the full set for every prompt tweak? it's expensive.
[05:06] Liam Patel: good question - we usually do a smoke-run for the changed templates (subset ~10% of prompts) and a full run weekly or on major model changes. for the pilot we can run the full set every Monday, smoke runs after any change.
[05:20] Dr. Sarah Thompson: can we get the full run artifacts and the diff report? the CSVs were helpful last week.
[05:27] Maya Chen: yes, we'll attach the full CSV and the diff report to the shared drive.
[05:32] (short pause, background noise)
[05:45] Rajiv Menon: also noticed the reranker had different orderings, were you changing the embedding model?
[05:52] Liam Patel: we moved from embed-16 to embed-20 for better semantics; that can reorder retrieval ranks slightly. If ordering is critical, we can pin the embed model or post-filter by clinical heuristics.
[06:05] Emily Park: for now we need stable ordering for top-3 cites, so let's pin embed-16 for the pilot.
[06:12] Maya Chen: noted. Liam - can you pin embeddings to embed-16 for the next run?
[06:16] Liam Patel: will do.
[06:18] Tom Alvarez: security - can you confirm SOC 2 status and whether we can get an SOC report?
[06:24] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we'll share the redacted report and the security questionnaire.
[06:31] Tom Alvarez: and about data residency - some records must stay in us-east-1, can we route regionally?
[06:37] Maya Chen: yes, region routing is supported. for pilot you're in us-east-1 already?
[06:41] Dr. Sarah Thompson: currently all pilot traffic was us-east but our EHR is us-west, so latency was slightly higher. we can switch.
[06:49] Liam Patel: switching region is a config flip, but we'll need to re-run the latency benchmarks. note dedicated capacity is better if you need sustained throughput, hosted is fine for bursty test traffic.
[07:02] Rajiv Menon: cost question - what's the delta for moving to dedicated pool with 4 GPUs?
[07:07] Maya Chen: rough estimate in the pricing sheet - about 40% higher than hosted at low utilization but gives predictable latency and reserved capacity. we'll send detailed numbers.
[07:16] Emily Park: back to quality - can we agree immediate mitigations?
[07:20] Dr. Sarah Thompson: yes, proposed mitigations: 1) revert the STOP_TOKEN change for discharge prompts, 2) pin embed model, 3) run smoke test only on patch routes, 4) add rule-based drug-interaction flag, 5) export guardrail logs to their S3.
[07:36] Liam Patel: agree. I'll revert STOP_TOKEN and re-run locally on the failing samples, pin embed-16, and add rule checks.
[07:44] Maya Chen: we'll also update the scoring thresholds for the annotator batch to reflect small variance and avoid false alarm.
[07:52] Ava Gomez: I'll prepare the export for guardrail logs and the SOC doc package.
[07:58] (overlap / slight crosstalk)
[08:05] Dr. Sarah Thompson: timeline - can we have a smoke-run and diff by Friday EOD?
[08:10] Liam Patel: yes, Friday EOD.
[08:13] Rajiv Menon: and then schedule a production-readiness walk on Monday?
[08:17] Maya Chen: Monday works. we'll put a calendar invite.
[08:21] Emily Park: please include the product and compliance folks.
[08:24] Tom Alvarez: and I want the audit logs in S3 before the Monday readout.
[08:29] Maya Chen: noted.
[08:31] (wrap-up)
[08:35] Maya Chen: quick recap: Liam revert stop token and run smoke tests, pin embed-16, add the drug-interaction rule; Ava share guardrail logs and SOC 2 package; Maya send pricing delta for dedicated and the diff CSV; schedule production-readiness call Monday.
[08:52] Dr. Sarah Thompson: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[08:55] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts. bye.

Potential transcription notes: occasional mislabels (screen-share noise), some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "rwd-47b-1.2q" may appear as "rw d 47 b 1.2 q"), timestamps approximate.
